description: The bar chart, titled "RoBERTa Size," compares the GLUE performance of different fine-tuning methods across two model sizes: "base" and "large." The horizontal axis displays seven fine-tuning methods: Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S₁-model, S₄-model, and S₅-model. The vertical axis represents GLUE Performance, scaled from 86 to 88. For each method, two bars are shown: a blue bar for the "base" model and a brown bar for the "large" model. The chart illustrates that the "large" model consistently outperforms the "base" model across all methods. The highest performance is achieved by the "S₅-model" with the "large" model, reaching a GLUE performance of approximately 89.2. The "LoRA" method with the "large" model also shows high performance, at about 89.0. In contrast, the lowest performance is observed with the "Adaptor" method using the "base" model, at approximately 86.2. The performance of the "base" model generally increases with the complexity of the method (e.g., from "Prefix" to "S₅-model"), while the "large" model shows a more varied trend, with "LoRA" and "S₅-model" achieving the highest scores.
